He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball|Marquette Golden Eagles]]. He is the son of former NBA player [[Wes Matthews]].{{cite web|title=Born to Play with a Former NBA Player as His Father, and an Ex-UW Standout as His Mother, Wesley Matthews Was|url=http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1G1-114070369.html|journal=The Wisconsin State Journal|date=July 14, 2014|access-date=March 3, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714223729/http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1G1-114070369.html|archive-date=14 July 2014|via=[[HighBeam Research]]|url-access=subscription|location=Madison, WI|url-status=usurped}} ==Early life== Matthews was born in San Antonio, Texas to [[Wes Matthews|Wesley Sr.]], a former NBA point guard and two-time [[List of NBA champions|NBA champion]] with the [[1987 NBA Finals|1987]] and [[1988 NBA Finals|1988]] [[Los Angeles Lakers]], and Pam Moore, an All-American runner and basketball player. Matthews starred on the [[James Madison Memorial High School]] basketball and soccer teams. He was named [[Wisconsin Mr. Basketball]] in 2005.{{cite news|last=Punzel|first=Dennis|title=Matthews feeling at home in Madison|work=Racine Journal Times|date=October 8, 2016|url=https://journaltimes.com/matthews-feeling-at-home-in-madison/article_59671017-d6a4-5be2-b460-dee29062c6aa.html|access-date=November 19, 2020}} ==College career== Matthews chose to attend [[Marquette University]] despite being pressured to play for the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]] like his father. Wesley was the biggest of the "three amigos", the three guards in the starting lineup for Marquette. This trio, [[Dominic James (basketball)|Dominic James]], [[Jerel McNeal]], and Matthews, started nearly every game together from their first year onwards. With the lack of height in the 2008–09 season at Marquette, Matthews learned to play against bigger opponents. He grabbed 13 rebounds in a Marquette 48-point win over [[NCAA Division II|Division II]] opponent [[Lewis Flyers]] on December 28, 2005.{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/253620269|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211224064600/https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/253620269|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 24, 2021|title=Lewis vs. Marquette - Game Recap - December 28, 2005 |website=ESPN.com|access-date=March 3, 2022}} In a game against the [[Tennessee Volunteers]] on December 16, 2008, Matthews scored a career-high{{Cite web|url=https://areyouwatchingthis.com/ncaab/games/91089|title=Marquette(23) 68, Tennessee(19) 80 - 12/17/2008 - Men's College Basketball|website=Areyouwatchingthis.com|access-date=March 3, 2022}} 30 points, making 15 of 18 [[free throw]]s.{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/283512633|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211224064604/https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/283512633|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 24, 2021|title=Marquette vs. Tennessee - Game Recap - December 16, 2008 |website=ESPN.com|access-date=March 3, 2022}} On January 7, 2009, he set a school record for field goal accuracy (minimum 10 attempts) when he went 10-for-10 en route to 23 points in an 81–76 win over [[Rutgers University|Rutgers]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/290070164|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211224064559/https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/290070164|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 24, 2021|title=Marquette vs. Rutgers - Game Recap - January 7, 2009 |website=ESPN.com|access-date=March 3, 2022}} ==Professional basketball career== ===Utah Jazz (2009–2010)=== After completing four years at Marquette, Matthews entered the [[2009 NBA draft]], but went undrafted. He joined the Utah Jazz for the Orlando Summer League and the Sacramento Kings for the Las Vegas Summer League. In September 2009, he signed a one-year deal with the Jazz. In February 2010, after the team's trade of [[Ronnie Brewer]], head coach [[Jerry Sloan]] made Matthews the team's starting shooting guard. The following month, on March 14, Matthews scored a then-career-high 29 points, including six made three-point shots, in a 119–111 loss to the Oklahoma City Thunder.{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.co.uk/nba/game/_/gameId/300314025|title=Jazz vs. Thunder - Game Summary - March 14, 2010|website=ESPN.com|access-date=March 3, 2022}} On June 29, 2010, the Jazz extended Matthews the league-specified qualifying offer, thereby making him a restricted free agent and giving the Jazz the opportunity to match any other free agent offer.{{cite web | title=Jazz make qualifying offers to pair |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=5340118 | publisher=ESPN | date=June 29, 2010 | access-date=June 29, 2010}} ===Portland Trail Blazers (2010–2015)=== On July 10, 2010, the Trail Blazers signed Matthews to a five-year, $34 million offer sheet.{{cite web | title=Trail Blazers sign free agent guard Wesley Matthews to 5-year, $34 million offer sheet |url=http://blog.oregonlive.com/behindblazersbeat/2010/07/trail_blazers_sign_free_agent.html | work=The Oregonian | date=July 10, 2010 | access-date=July 10, 2010}} On July 21, 2010, following the Jazz's decision not to match the Trail Blazers' offer sheet, Matthews officially signed the five-year, $34 million contract.{{cite web | title=Matthews signs with Trail Blazers |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=5398557 | publisher=ESPN | date=July 21, 2010 | access-date=July 21, 2010}} In his first season with Portland, Matthews averaged 15.9 points per game, and his three-point shot improved from 38 percent to 41 percent. After [[Brandon Roy]] began missing time due to knee problems, Matthews gained a spot in the Blazers' starting lineup. The durable Matthews played in 250 consecutive NBA games before being forced to sit out of a game on December 10, 2012, due to an injury to his left hip.Joe Freeman, [http://www.oregonlive.com/blazers/index.ssf/2012/12/wesley_matthews_iron_man_streak_will_end_tonight_w.html "Wesley Matthews' Iron Man Streak Will End Tonight When Blazers Host Toronto"], ''The Oregonian'', December 10, 2012. Matthews' ability and willingness to play through minor injuries and pain earned him the nickname "Iron Man", an appellation used by Trail Blazers fans, television and radio commentators, and arena public address announcers alike.Dane Carbaugh, [http://www.sportingnews.com/nba/story/2014-10-29/portland-trail-blazers-wesley-matthews-brandon-roy-career-stats-contract-salary "Most Known Unknown: Wesley Matthews and the Portland Trail Blazers"], ''The Sporting News'', October 30, 2014. On November 23, 2013, in a game against the [[Golden State Warriors]], Matthews was involved in an altercation and was ejected along with teammate, [[Mo Williams]]. He scored 23 points in 25 minutes of action before leaving the game. On November 25 it was announced that he was fined $20,000.{{cite news | title=Mo Williams Suspended, LaMarcus Aldridge & Wesley Matthews Fined After Scrum Between Blazers & Warriors |url=http://www.blazersedge.com/2013/11/25/5144870/mo-williams-suspended-lamarcus-aldridge-wesley-matthews-fined-after | website=Blazersedge.com| date=November 25, 2013 | access-date=November 25, 2013}} On January 17, 2015, Matthews became the Trail Blazers all-time career leader in three-point field goals made, surpassing [[Terry Porter]]'s franchise record of 773.{{cite web | title=Wesley Matthews passes Terry Porter for most 3-pointers made in Trail Blazers history |url=http://www.oregonlive.com/blazers/index.ssf/2015/01/wesley_matthews_passes_terry_porter_for_most_3-poi.html | access-date=January 17, 2015}} On March 5, 2015, in a game against the [[Dallas Mavericks]], Matthews tore his left achilles tendon and was subsequently ruled out for the rest of the season.{{cite web | last=Wojnarowski | first=Adrian | title=Wesley Matthews to miss rest of season with torn Achilles tendon |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/news/sources--wesley-matthews-to-miss-rest-of-season-with-torn-achilles-tendon-061418771.html | publisher=Yahoo! | date=March 5, 2015 | access-date=March 5, 2015}} ===Dallas Mavericks (2015–2019)=== On July 9, 2015, Matthews signed a four-year, $70 million deal with the [[Dallas Mavericks]].{{Cite web|date=2015-07-09|title=Source: Matthews' deal with Mavs grows to $70M|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/13229891/wesley-matthews-contract-dallas-mavericks-increases-deandre-jordan-reversed-commitment-team|access-date=2020-11-21|website=ESPN.com|language=en}} On December 6, 2015, he scored 28 of his season-high 36 points in the second half of the Mavericks' 116–104 win over the [[Washington Wizards]]. He hit 10 three-pointers in the game, with eight of them coming in the second half.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151206/DALWAS/gameinfo.html|title=Matthews scores 36 points, Mavericks beat Wizards 116–104|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=December 6, 2015|access-date=December 6, 2015}} On November 30, 2016, Matthews scored a season-high 26 points in a 94–87 loss to the [[San Antonio Spurs]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899722|title=Mills helps Spurs rally to beat Mavericks 94–87|publisher=ESPN|date=November 30, 2016|access-date=December 1, 2016}} He tied that mark three times in early December.{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/m/matthwe02/gamelog/2017/|title=Wesley Matthews 2016–17 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=November 19, 2017}} Matthews set a new season high on February 3, 2017, scoring 27 points in a 108–104 win over the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900159|title=Ferrell leads Mavericks to 108–104 win over Trail Blazers|publisher=ESPN|date=February 3, 2017|access-date=November 19, 2017}} On November 18, 2017, Matthews scored a season-high 22 points in a 111–79 win over the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400974984|title=Mavericks stop 4-game slide with win 24, 2018, he matched a pair of season highs with 29 points and seven 3-pointers in a 104–97 loss to the [[Houston Rockets]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975452|title=Harden, Rockets make it 6 straight over Mavs with 104–97 win|publisher=ESPN|date=January 24, 2018|access-date=January 24, 2018}} On February 13, 2018, in a 114–109 loss to [[Sacramento Kings]], Matthews 2018|access-date=April 30, 2018}} In January 2019, Matthews became the sixth player in Mavericks history to make 600 3-pointers,{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071337|title=Spurs rally from 19 down, beat Mavs 105–101|publisher=ESPN|date=January 16, 2019|access-date=January 17, 2019|quote=Matthews became the 3-pointers.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071411|title=Leonard scores 33 as Raptors beat Doncic, Mavericks 123–120|publisher=ESPN|date=January 27, 2019|access-date=January 27, 2019}} ===New York Knicks (2019)=== On January 31, 2019, Matthews was traded to the [[New York Knicks]] in a multiplayer trade.{{cite web |title=Knicks Acquire Dennis Smith Jr., Deandre Jordan, Wesley Matthews, and Two Future First round Picks |url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/front-office-news/knicks-acquire-dennis-smith-jr-deandre-jordan-wesley-matthews-from-dallas |publisher=National Basketball Association |access-date=January 31, 2019}} On February 7, Matthews was waived by the Knicks after appearing in just two games for the team.{{Cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/article/2019/02/07/new-york-knicks-wesley-matthews-enes-kanter|title=Knicks waive Wesley Matthews, Enes Kanter|date=February 7, 2019|publisher=National Basketball Association|access-date=February 7, 2019}} ===Indiana Pacers (2019)=== On February 10, 2019, Matthews signed with the [[Indiana Pacers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-sign-wesley-matthews|title=Pacers Sign Wesley Matthews|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=February 10, 2019|access-date=February 10, 2019}} On February 22, Matthews made 6 three-pointers and finished with 24 points, to lead the Pacers in a comeback win over the [[New Orleans Pelicans]]. ===Milwaukee Bucks (2019–2020)=== On July 12, 2019, Matthews signed with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].{{cite web|title=Bucks Sign Robin Lopez and Wes Matthews|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/bucks-sign-robin-lopez-and-wes-matthews|website=NBA.com|access-date=July 12, 2019|date=July 12, 2019}} On November 25, 2019, Matthews scored 19 points and grabbed 4 rebounds while starting in place of injured All-Star [[Khris Middleton]] in a game against the [[Utah Jazz]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/201911250MIL.html|title = Utah Jazz at Milwaukee Bucks Box Score|date=November 25, 2019|website=Basketball-Reference.com}} On December 22, he again scored 19 points, this time in a win against his previous team, the Pacers.{{Cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/201912220MIL.html|title = Indiana Pacers at Milwaukee Bucks Box Score|date=December 22, 2019|website=Basketball-Reference.com}} ===Los Angeles Lakers (2020–2021)=== On November 22, 2020, Matthews signed with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{cite web|title=Lakers Sign Wesley Matthews|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/lakers-sign-wesley-matthews-2021-free-agency|website=NBA.com|access-date=November 22, 2020|date=November 22, 2020}} He appeared in 58 games for the Lakers, averaging only 4.8 points and a career-worst 33% 3-point shot percentage.{{Cite web|url=https://www.si.com/nba/lakers/news/lakers-news-should-the-lakers-re-sign-wesley-matthews|title = Lakers News: Should the Lakers Re-Sign Wesley Matthews?|website=Si.com}} ===Return to Milwaukee (2021–2023)=== On December 3, 2021, Matthews was signed by the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].{{cite web|title=Milwaukee Bucks Sign Wesley Matthews|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/milwaukee-bucks-sign-wesley-matthews|website=NBA.com|date=December 3, 2021|access-date=December 3, 2021}} During Milwaukee's Christmas Day game, Matthews scored just 9 points, but gave the Bucks the lead by making a 3-point shot with 30 seconds left to help complete a 19-point come back, in a 117–113 win over the [[Boston Celtics]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/nba/bucks/2021/12/25/milwaukee-bucks-vs-boston-celtics-fiserv-forum-game-updates/9005555002/|title = Bucks 117, Celtics 113: Giannis Antetokounmpo returns to lead a 19-point comeback victory|website=Jsonline.com}}{{Cite news|url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/nba/bucks/2022/01/04/wesley-matthews-reunion-milwaukee-bucks-working-out/9087573002/|title=For Wesley Matthews and the Milwaukee Bucks, the reunion was worth the wait|first=Jim|last=Owczarski|newspaper=[[Milwaukee Journal Sentinel]]|access-date=March 3, 2022}} Matthews was inserted into the starting lineup by [[Mike Budenholzer]] towards the end of the regular season to provide a defensive presence alongside [[NBA All-Defensive Team|All-Defensive]] guard [[Jrue Holiday]]. On July 6, 2022, Matthews re-signed with the Bucks.{{Cite web |title=Milwaukee Bucks Re-Sign Wesley Matthews |url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/milwaukee-bucks-re-sign-wesley-matthews |access-date=2022-07-12 |website=www.nba.com |language=en}} ===Atlanta Hawks (2023–2024)=== On July 22, 2023, Matthews signed with the [[Atlanta Hawks]].{{cite web|title=Atlanta Hawks Sign Guard Wesley Matthews|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-sign-guard-wesley-matthews|website=NBA.com|date=July 22, 2023|access-date=July 23, 2023}} ==Post-playing career== Matthews began a career as a broadcaster/analyst with his former team, the Milwaukee Bucks, and [[FanDuel Sports Network]] for 35 games in the 2025-26 season alongside play-by-play announcer [[Lisa Byington]].{{cite news |title=Weigel Announces Expanded Access to Milwaukee Bucks Games for 2025-26 Season {{!}} Milwaukee Bucks
